questions.question: What is the highest-grossing film of all time globally (unadjusted for inflation)?
questions.explanation: James Cameron's 2009 sci-fi epic Avatar has grossed over $2.92 Billion worldwide across multiple re-releases.
questions.funFact: James Cameron waited over 10 years to film Avatar until 3D camera technology caught up with his vision!

questions.question: Which superhero movie won Heath Ledger a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor?
questions.explanation: Heath Ledger won the Oscar for his iconic performance as the Joker in Christopher Nolan's 2008 masterpiece The Dark Knight.
questions.funFact: Heath Ledger spent a month locked alone in a London hotel room developing the Joker's eerie voice, mannerisms, and diary!

questions.question: In the Netflix smash-hit 'Stranger Things', what is the name of the parallel dark dimension?
questions.explanation: The dark alternate reflection of Hawkins, Indiana is known throughout the series as The Upside Down.
questions.funFact: The Duffer Brothers initially pitched the show under the working title 'Montauk'!

questions.question: How many Oscars did Titanic win at the 1998 ceremony, tying the record?
questions.explanation: Titanic won 11 Oscars, tying Ben-Hur (1959) for the record, later matched by The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King.
questions.funFact: Titanic was the first film ever to gross over $1 billion.

questions.question: Which director made both Titanic and Avatar?
questions.explanation: James Cameron directed both films, which each held the title of the highest-grossing film ever.
questions.funFact: He also directed The Terminator and Aliens.

questions.question: Which 1975 film directed by Steven Spielberg is often called the first summer blockbuster?
questions.explanation: Jaws' huge success in summer 1975 changed how Hollywood released big films.
questions.funFact: The mechanical shark, nicknamed Bruce, often broke down during filming.

questions.question: Who directed the original Star Wars, released in 1977?
questions.explanation: George Lucas wrote and directed Star Wars: A New Hope, launching one of the biggest franchises ever.
questions.funFact: It opened in only about 32 theatres at first.

questions.question: Which actor delivered the line 'I'll be back' in The Terminator (1984)?
questions.explanation: Schwarzenegger's Terminator says the line to a police desk officer before returning in a car.
questions.funFact: Schwarzenegger reportedly has fewer than 20 lines in the film.

questions.question: Which Hogwarts house is Harry Potter sorted into?
questions.explanation: Harry is sorted into Gryffindor, the house known for bravery.
questions.funFact: The Sorting Hat considered putting him in Slytherin.

questions.question: Which film in 2008 began the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
questions.explanation: Iron Man, starring Robert Downey Jr., launched the MCU.
questions.funFact: Iron Man's famous final line 'I am Iron Man' was reportedly ad-libbed.

questions.question: In which Marvel movie does Thanos snap his fingers and turn half of all life to dust?
questions.explanation: Thanos completes the Infinity Gauntlet and uses it at the end of Infinity War (2018).
questions.funFact: Infinity War and Endgame were filmed back to back.

questions.question: Which superhero film became the first to be nominated for the Best Picture Oscar?
questions.explanation: Black Panther (2018) became the first superhero film nominated for Best Picture, at the 2019 Oscars.
questions.funFact: The character first appeared in Marvel comics in 1966.

questions.question: Which film became the first non-English-language movie to win Best Picture at the Oscars?
questions.explanation: South Korea's Parasite, directed by Bong Joon-ho, won Best Picture at the 2020 ceremony.
questions.funFact: It also won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2019.

questions.question: Which film won Best Picture at the Oscars in 2024?
questions.explanation: Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer won seven Oscars including Best Picture and Best Director.
questions.funFact: It was released the same day as Barbie, creating the 'Barbenheimer' phenomenon.

questions.question: Which song from RRR won the Oscar for Best Original Song in 2023?
questions.explanation: 'Naatu Naatu,' composed by M. M. Keeravani, became the first song from an Indian film to win the Oscar.
questions.funFact: The song was filmed in Ukraine near the presidential palace in Kyiv.

questions.question: Which composer won two Oscars for the 2008 film Slumdog Millionaire?
questions.explanation: A. R. Rahman won Best Original Score and Best Original Song for 'Jai Ho'.
questions.funFact: Rahman is nicknamed the 'Mozart of Madras'.

questions.question: Which Indian filmmaker, director of Pather Panchali, received an honorary Oscar in 1992?
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray was awarded an Academy Honorary Award for lifetime achievement shortly before his death.
questions.funFact: He reportedly pawned his wife's jewellery to fund Pather Panchali.

questions.question: Which Aamir Khan film was nominated for the Best Foreign Language Film Oscar at the 2002 ceremony?
questions.explanation: Lagaan, a cricket drama set in colonial India, was nominated at the 74th Academy Awards.
questions.funFact: It was the third Indian film ever to be nominated in that category.

questions.question: In which 1975 film do Jai and Veeru fight the dacoit Gabbar Singh?
questions.explanation: Sholay starred Amitabh Bachchan and Dharmendra, with Amjad Khan as the villain Gabbar Singh.
questions.funFact: It reportedly ran for five years continuously in a Mumbai theatre.

questions.question: Which Bollywood film ran for over 20 years at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir theatre?
questions.explanation: DDLJ (1995), starring Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol, played at Maratha Mandir for about 25 years.
questions.funFact: The film's Raj and Simran remain iconic romantic figures in Indian cinema.

questions.question: Which actor is known by the nickname 'King Khan' or 'Badshah of Bollywood'?
questions.explanation: Shah Rukh Khan earned the title over decades of blockbuster romances and action films.
questions.funFact: He began his career on TV with the serial Fauji in 1988.

questions.question: Which 2017 film became the first Indian film to gross over Rs 1,000 crore?
questions.explanation: Baahubali 2 crossed the 1,000 crore mark within about ten days of release.
questions.funFact: 'Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?' became one of India's biggest cinema questions.

questions.question: What does 'Bollywood' get its name from?
questions.explanation: The name blends Bombay (now Mumbai), home of Hindi cinema, and Hollywood.
questions.funFact: India produces more films per year than any other country.

questions.question: Rajinikanth, known as 'Superstar', was born in which city and once worked there as a bus conductor?
questions.explanation: Rajinikanth was born Shivaji Rao Gaekwad in Bengaluru and worked as a BMTC bus conductor before entering films.
questions.funFact: He got his first break with K. Balachander in Tamil cinema.

questions.question: KGF: Chapter 1 (2018) belongs to which film industry?
questions.explanation: KGF, starring Yash, put Kannada cinema on the pan-Indian map.
questions.funFact: KGF stands for Kolar Gold Fields, in Karnataka.

questions.question: What is the name of the coffee shop in Friends?
questions.explanation: Central Perk is where the six friends meet in New York on the show.
questions.funFact: Friends ran for ten seasons from 1994 to 2004.

questions.question: In Game of Thrones, which house has the motto 'Winter Is Coming'?
questions.explanation: House Stark of Winterfell use the words as their motto.
questions.funFact: The show ended in 2019 after eight seasons.

questions.question: What is Walter White's job at the start of Breaking Bad?
questions.explanation: Walter White, played by Bryan Cranston, is a chemistry teacher who starts making meth.
questions.funFact: The show is set in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

questions.question: The Netflix hit Squid Game is from which country?
questions.explanation: Squid Game, created by Hwang Dong-hyuk, became a global phenomenon in 2021.
questions.funFact: Hwang reportedly spent about a decade trying to get the show made.

questions.question: In Money Heist, what do the robbers wear as masks?
questions.explanation: The gang wears red jumpsuits and Salvador Dali masks.
questions.funFact: The Spanish show was originally aired on Antena 3 before Netflix picked it up.

questions.question: Which long-running animated TV show is set in the town of Springfield?
questions.explanation: The Simpsons premiered as a series in 1989 and is the longest-running American animated series.
questions.funFact: It started as short cartoons on The Tracey Ullman Show.

questions.question: Which Michael Jackson album (1982) is widely credited as the best-selling album ever?
questions.explanation: Thriller is estimated to have sold around 70 million copies worldwide.
questions.funFact: It won a record eight Grammys in 1984.

questions.question: From which English city did The Beatles come?
questions.explanation: The Beatles formed in Liverpool in 1960, started as The Quarrymen.
questions.funFact: They had 20 number-one hits on the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.question: Which Taylor Swift tour became the first to gross over $1 billion?
questions.explanation: The Eras Tour (2023-2024) became the highest-grossing concert tour ever, at over $2 billion.
questions.funFact: The tour had over 140 shows.

questions.question: Which Korean group's 'Dynamite' made them the first Korean act to top the Billboard Hot 100 in 2020?
questions.explanation: BTS topped the chart in September 2020 with 'Dynamite'.
questions.funFact: BTS stands for Bangtan Sonyeondan, or 'Bulletproof Boy Scouts'.

questions.question: Which actor won the Best Actor Oscar for playing Freddie Mercury in Bohemian Rhapsody?
questions.explanation: Rami Malek won Best Actor at the 2019 Oscars for the Queen biopic.
questions.funFact: He wore prosthetic teeth to play Mercury.

questions.question: Which singer is known as 'The King of Rock and Roll'?
questions.explanation: Elvis Presley, from Memphis, became a global icon in the 1950s.
questions.funFact: His home Graceland is in Memphis, Tennessee.

questions.question: Which 1995 film was the first entirely computer-animated feature film?
questions.explanation: Pixar's Toy Story was the first full-length computer-animated feature.
questions.funFact: Early drafts had Woody as a much nastier character.

questions.question: What is the name of the snowman in Disney's Frozen?
questions.explanation: Olaf, voiced by Josh Gad, is a snowman brought to life by Elsa's magic.
questions.funFact: Olaf loves warm hugs and summer.

questions.question: The Lion King's story is loosely inspired by which Shakespeare play?
questions.explanation: Simba's story of a young prince and a usurping uncle echoes Hamlet.
questions.funFact: 'Simba' means 'lion' in Swahili.

questions.question: Which animated film won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2002?
questions.explanation: DreamWorks' Shrek won the very first Oscar in the new category.
questions.funFact: Mike Myers re-recorded Shrek's voice with a Scottish accent.

questions.question: Which actor plays Tony Stark/Iron Man in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
questions.explanation: Robert Downey Jr. played Tony Stark from 2008 to Avengers: Endgame in 2019.
questions.funFact: Iron Man's suit was a huge part of the film's effects.

questions.question: For which film did Leonardo DiCaprio finally win his Best Actor Oscar in 2016?
questions.explanation: DiCaprio won for playing frontiersman Hugh Glass in The Revenant.
questions.funFact: He had been nominated several times before winning.

questions.question: Which actor holds the record for the most Academy Award nominations?
questions.explanation: Meryl Streep has been nominated more than 20 times and has won three Oscars.
questions.funFact: She won for Kramer vs. Kramer, Sophie's Choice and The Iron Lady.

questions.question: In The Matrix, which pill does Neo take to learn the truth?
questions.explanation: Morpheus offers Neo a choice, and Neo takes the red pill.
questions.funFact: The film's 'bullet time' effect was hugely influential.

questions.question: In Inception, what object does Cobb spin to check whether he is dreaming?
questions.explanation: Cobb's totem is a spinning top, which would keep spinning in a dream.
questions.funFact: The film ends with the top's fate unresolved.

questions.question: In Jurassic Park, from what do scientists extract dinosaur DNA?
questions.explanation: The park's scientists took dinosaur blood from mosquitoes preserved in amber.
questions.funFact: The T. rex roar was a mix of animal sounds, including a baby elephant.

questions.question: Which 2009 Bollywood film made 'Aal Izz Well' a household phrase?
questions.explanation: 3 Idiots, starring Aamir Khan, made the phrase a national catchphrase.
questions.funFact: It was loosely based on Chetan Bhagat's novel Five Point Someone.

questions.question: Which TV quiz show, hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, is India's version of 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?'
questions.explanation: KBC premiered in 2000, and Amitabh Bachchan is its best-known host.
questions.funFact: 'Lock kiya jaye' became a famous catchphrase.

questions.question: Which 1973 film established Amitabh Bachchan's 'Angry Young Man' persona?
questions.explanation: Zanjeer, directed by Prakash Mehra, made Bachchan a star as the intense police inspector Vijay.
questions.funFact: All India Radio once rejected him because of his voice.
